title: The projective-line adjunction for towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and an arbitrary scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and their ordinary derived category [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. For a scheme $T$ over $S$, write $\mathscr C^+(T)$ for the full subcategory of $D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ whose level $n$, for every $n\geq1$, is in the essential image of $\nu_T^*:D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)\to D^+(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)$; this means there exists an etale-origin witness as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Write $\mathbf P^1_T=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};T)$ as in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Let $\Delta:\mathbf P^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ be the diagonal.

Let $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, and let $p_1,p_2:\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S\to\mathbf P^1_S$
be the projections. Define, for $K_\bullet\in\mathscr C^+(S)$ and
$M_\bullet\in\mathscr C^+(\mathbf P^1_S)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet):\ &Rq_{*,\bullet}(q_\bullet^*K_\bullet(1)[2])
\simeq K_\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rq_{*,\bullet}(\mathcal O_{E,\mathbf P^1_S}/\ell^\bullet)(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{id}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}\ }K_\bullet,\\
\eta_\bullet(M_\bullet):\ &M_\bullet\simeq Rp_{2*,\bullet}\Delta_*M_\bullet
\xrightarrow{\ Rp_{2*,\bullet}(\delta_\bullet\otimes p_1^*M_\bullet)\ }
Rp_{2*,\bullet}p_1^*M_\bullet(1)[2]\simeq q_\bullet^*Rq_{*,\bullet}M_\bullet(1)[2],
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}$ and $\delta_\bullet$ from [det-sp-tower-classes].
Then $\eta_\bullet$ and $\varepsilon_\bullet$ are the unit and counit of an
adjunction $Rq_{*,\bullet}\dashv q_\bullet^*(-)(1)[2]$ between $\mathscr C^+(\mathbf P^1_S)$ and $\mathscr C^+(S)$, whose
evaluation at level $n$ is the finite projective-line adjunction. In the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], where $S$ is separated and of finite type over a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, this adjunction restricts to the full subcategories of uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor towers [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers].

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, $W=P\times_SP$, $A_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^\bullet$, $F=Rq_{*,\bullet}$ and $G=q_\bullet^*(-)(1)[2]$. By [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels], these direct images are bounded below and evaluate to the finite direct images. The canonical comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] applies to $q,p_1,p_2,\Delta$, which are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and therefore their direct images preserve etale-origin levels. Pullback preserves such levels by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The finite twist is a locally free rank-one sheaf, compatible with pullback, by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] with $N=\ell^n$ and $A=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Thus $F,G$ preserve the stated bounded-below etale-origin domains.

Each of $q,p_1,p_2$ is a projective-line projection, hence proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. The diagonal is a closed Cartier divisor by [det-sp-tower-classes], hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). Its complementary open is quasi-compact: over each affine open of $W$, finitely many principal opens trivialize the invertible ideal, and the complement on each is one more principal open. Thus [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] makes $\Delta_*$ exact at every finite level. Exactness on towers is levelwise by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], so $R\Delta_{*,\bullet}=\Delta_*$, justifying the notation in the unit formula.

source.place: Construction: properness and exact diagonal direct image

proof.text: Form the canonical tensor, projection, composition and exchange maps on the simultaneous section models [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. These exist in the ambient unbounded derived category and evaluate to their finite maps. At level $n$, put $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. On the ordinary etale site, [lem-kun-0f0g] makes the projection maps for $q,p_1,p_2,\Delta$ invertible for these coefficients and arbitrary derived inputs. For the present etale-origin inputs, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to $\nu^*$ transports tensor, and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] transports the direct images of the bounded-below arguments. The canonical comparisons transport the projection map itself: both maps are the transpose of the same counit tensored with identity, so the normalization in the direct-image comparison identifies their transposes. The finite etale projection identities also show that the tensors occurring here are bounded below: their targets are respectively $Rq_*q^{-1}K(1)[2]$, $R\Delta_*M$, or $Rp_{i*}p_i^{-1}M(1)[2]$. For the last two projection reorderings, $Rp_{i*}B_W(1)[2]$ is a sum of two shifted flat lines by [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals], so its tensor with $M$ is bounded below. Proper exchange is invertible by [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring], and the same counit-mate normalization transports its actual map. Hence every evaluated projection and exchange map used here is invertible. Tower evaluation detects isomorphisms by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](3), so the actual tower maps are invertible. This avoids applying that node's restricted finite-Tor projection clause outside its hypotheses.

source.place: Construction: canonical projection and exchange on the stated domain

proof.text: The projection isomorphism for $\Delta$, with $\Delta^*p_1^*M=M$, identifies $\Delta_*M$ with $\Delta_*A_P\otimes^Lp_1^*M$. Exchange identifies $Rp_{2*,\bullet}p_1^*M$ with $q_\bullet^*FM$, and the projection formula for $q$ identifies $FGK$ with $K\otimes^LRq_{*,\bullet}A_P(1)[2]$, as in step 3. Composing with the actual diagonal class and trace of [det-sp-tower-classes] gives precisely the displayed natural $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$. Their naturality and evaluations follow from [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $t_i=\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i,\bullet}$. Under exchange $t_i$ is the base change of the trace for $q$: the splitting components are the unit and $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; pullback preserves the unit, pulls back $\mathcal O(1)$, and commutes with the Kummer boundary. It therefore carries the splitting, its inverse, and its second projection to those on the base change. This is an identity of the actual tower constructions, not an inference of equality from evaluation.

source.place: Construction of unit and counit; base change of the splitting trace

proof.text: *The two scalar endomorphisms and detection.* Let $\alpha_i:A_P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{i*,\bullet}\Delta_*A_P$ be the composition identification for $p_i\Delta=1_P$, and put $c_i=t_i\circ Rp_{i*,\bullet}(\delta_\bullet)\circ\alpha_i$. These are endomorphisms of $A_P[0]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to the abelian tower category of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]: each $c_i$ is a unique compatible family of module-sheaf maps. If all evaluated $c_i$ are identities, their underlying families equal the identity family, so $c_i=1$. This uses equality detection only between these degree-zero objects. The composition identification is the canonical derived-direct-image comparison supplied on tower section models by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Fix $n\geq1$ and put $N=\ell^n$, $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. This is a finite torsion ring and $N$ is invertible on $S$. Exact evaluation and the canonical direct-image comparison identify the level of $c_i$ from step 5 with the pro-etale image of the finite etale composite $t_P\circ Rp_{i*}(\delta_B)\circ\alpha_i$: [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels] and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] identify the actual direct-image and composition maps, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] specifies the comparison, and [det-sp-tower-classes] identifies the evaluated splitting, trace and supported class. The finite identity is exactly [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals], which assumes neither a Noetherian nor a finite-type base. Applying $\nu_P^*$ gives $(c_i)_n=1$ for both $i$. Step 5 now gives $c_1=c_2=1$ in the ordinary derived category of towers.

*First triangle, integrating along $p_1$.* Expand $F\eta_M$ using its definition, replace $qp_2$ by $qp_1$, and then apply $\varepsilon_{FM}$. With the canonical direct-image composition maps and the projection formula established in step 3 this gives
$$FM=R(qp_1)_{*,\bullet}\Delta_*M\longrightarrow R(qp_1)_{*,\bullet}p_1^*M(1)[2]\simeq F\bigl(M\otimes^LRp_{1*,\bullet}A_W(1)[2]\bigr)\xrightarrow{F(1_M\otimes t_1)}FM.$$
Here $t_1$ is the base-changed trace identified in step 4. The first arrow is $\delta_\bullet\otimes p_1^*M$. Naturality of the projection comparison identifies its pushforward along $p_1$, including the source identification $\Delta^*p_1^*M=M$, with $1_M\otimes Rp_{1*,\bullet}\delta_\bullet$. The exchange and projection reordering is the equality in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the tower-topos ring object $A_\bullet$; [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] supplies the specified composition comparisons on this model. Thus the entire composite is $F(1_M\otimes c_1)=1_{FM}$ by step 6, rather than merely a map which becomes an identity on evaluation.

source.place: Reduction of the triangle identities: first triangle

proof.text: *Second triangle, integrating along $p_2$.* Put $M=GK$. On $W$ both $p_1^*M$ and $p_2^*M$ equal $(qp_1)^*K(1)[2]$, since $qp_1=qp_2$ and the twist pulls back from $S$. Factor $p_2^*M$ out of $Rp_{2*,\bullet}(A_W\otimes^Lp_2^*M)(1)[2]$ using the projection formula established in step 3. The arrow induced by $\delta_\bullet$ becomes $1_M\otimes Rp_{2*,\bullet}\delta_\bullet$, with source $M\otimes A_P$. Under proper exchange, $G\varepsilon_K$ contracts the remaining factor $Rp_{2*,\bullet}A_W(1)[2]$ by $t_2$, by step 4. The exchange/projection compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the same tower ringed topos verifies these are the canonical maps. Hence $G\varepsilon_K\circ\eta_{GK}=1_{GK}\otimes c_2=1_{GK}$. Only even shifts have been moved past tensor factors, so their Koszul signs are $(-1)^{2j}=1$. The interchange of the two unshifted twist lines is also the identity: locally choose a generator $e$; the symmetry sends $ae\otimes be$ to $be\otimes ae=ab(e\otimes e)$ over the commutative coefficient ring. These local equalities give the stated canonical symmetry globally.

source.place: Reduction of the triangle identities: second triangle

proof.text: *Adjunction from the two triangles.* For a tower map $u:FM\to K$ define $\Phi(u)=G(u)\circ\eta_M$, and for $v:M\to GK$ define $\Psi(v)=\varepsilon_K\circ F(v)$. Naturality and step 7 give $\Psi\Phi(u)=u\circ\varepsilon_{FM}\circ F\eta_M=u$. Naturality and step 8 give $\Phi\Psi(v)=G\varepsilon_K\circ\eta_{GK}\circ v=v$. These operations are natural in $M,K$, so they are the Hom bijection exhibiting $F\dashv G$ with the specified unit and counit.

*Evaluation and restriction.* For each $n\geq1$, exact evaluation sends $A_\bullet$ to $(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, sends $\delta_\bullet$ to the finite supported diagonal class, and sends the splitting inverse followed by its second projection to the finite trace, by [det-sp-tower-classes]. The specified tensor, direct-image, exchange and projection comparisons evaluate to their finite comparisons by the section models [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and the maps constructed in step 3; shifts and inverse image are termwise. Substituting these in the displayed formulas gives the finite diagonal-defined unit and splitting-trace-defined counit with the actual coefficients $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$.

source.place: Levels: evaluation of the specified maps

proof.text:
Here is an explicit verification that these maps form the finite adjunction on bounded-below etale-origin levels. Given a bounded-below complex $L$ of etale $B$-module sheaves on a scheme $T$, put $
u_T^*L$ at level $n$ and the zero complex at every other level, with every transition zero. This is a bounded-below complex of towers by the componentwise definition [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], and is in $\mathscr C^+(T)$. Denote its derived object by $J_nL$. Write $F_n=Rq_{*,B}$ and $G_n=q^{-1}(-)(1)[2]$ on the finite etale categories. Evaluate the first tower triangle of step 7 on $J_nM$, for arbitrary $M\in D^+(P_{\mathrm{et}},B)$: the specified comparisons give
$$
u_S^* igl(\varepsilon_{n,F_nM}\circ F_n(\eta_{n,M}) igr)=1_{
u_S^*F_nM}.$$
Evaluate the second tower triangle of step 8 on $J_nK$, for arbitrary $K\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},B)$: they give
$$
u_P^* igl(G_n(\varepsilon_{n,K})\circ\eta_{n,G_nK} igr)=1_{
u_P^*G_nK}.$$
Full faithfulness [sk-prop-sf-comparison] removes $
u^*$ from both equalities. Thus the finite maps satisfy both triangles for every finite bounded-below input. Explicitly the inverse Hom operations are $u\mapsto G_n(u)\eta_{n,M}$ and $v\mapsto\varepsilon_{n,K}F_n(v)$, whose composites are $u\varepsilon_{n,F_nM}F_n\eta_{n,M}=u$ and $G_n\varepsilon_{n,K}\eta_{n,G_nK}v=v$. This proves the finite adjunction over the arbitrary base using the evaluated maps.

source.place: Levels: finite triangles via single-level towers

proof.text: Now assume the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $S$ is separated and of finite type over a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\ne\ell$. To see that the full uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories lie in $\mathscr C^+$, use [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] locally on affine $U$ and [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] with [sk-prop-sf-comparison]: the classical cohomology condition is local, so the bounded-below equivalence gives a global etale-origin witness for each bounded constructible level. Uniform cohomological bounds give a bounded-below tower because tower cohomology and vanishing are levelwise [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian].

source.place: Restriction: the standing scheme setting and etale-origin witnesses

proof.text: [sk-lem-sp-tower-bound], with $f=q$, preserves uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor towers under $F$. The map $q$ is a separated finite-type morphism of the standing schemes, smooth of relative dimension one, so this application satisfies the hypotheses of [sk-lem-sp-tower-bound].

source.place: Restriction: preservation by the proper direct image

proof.text: For $G$ the bounds can be checked locally over each affine open $U\subseteq S$, where both $U$ and $\mathbf P^1_U$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. With $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$, the constructible comparison [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] gives a bounded constructible etale representative $L_n$ of $K_n|_U$. The same fixed Tor interval $[a,b]$ holds for $L_n$ by [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval]. Choose its flat representative supported in $[a,b]$ using [lem-sf-etale-flat-model]. A bounded complex of flat sheaves is K-flat: tensoring each flat term with an acyclic complex is acyclic, and the finite filtration by shifted terms gives the assertion for the complex. The termwise pullback along $q$ is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], and remains supported in $[a,b]$. Tensor with the locally free rank-one twist of [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] and shift by $[2]$ gives a flat complex supported in $[a-2,b-2]$; its tensor with any degree-zero test sheaf has no other terms, so this is its Tor interval. Transfer the interval back to the pro-etale site by [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval]. Exact inverse image preserves the cohomological interval, and inverse-image strata and their pulled-back finite constant trivializations show constructibility. These bounds hold for every $n$ and every $U$; vanishing is local, so they hold globally, with the shift moving both bounds by $-2$. Hence both functors preserve the full tower subcategories [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and the same Hom bijection restricts to them.
